quote: People brought the usual human pain and suffering with them, and it all got translated into politics.
heading: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly
said_already: Eventually, when people are together long enough, politics will become a way of carrying emotional material that people can’t name. [Outer-freedom-only models]

quote: But what I gathered from a bird’s eye view is that the secular communities often thought they could make everyone feel loved and respected by adopting optimal democratic procedures. The spiritual communities went deeper in search of real purpose, belonging, and divine connection, but often put one person in charge of everybody’s inner life. Most of my big little article here is me attempting to describe the missing bridge between those.
heading: The New Age May Dawn Suddenly
said_already: Most communes of my acquaintance traded inner freedom of the heart (spirituality) for outer freedom (secular, nondogmatic, political). The two pendulum ends of this trade-off mirror each other. I believe we can combine the best of both, but first, let’s see how each fails individually. [Why Communities Keep Dying in the Same Two Ways]

quote: It was chaotic, but sincere, and it revealed to me how people are so ready for this that they’ll literally jump into it from one video.
heading: Communes Are Hot Again 🔥
said_already: Later, when another influencer with a big following floated the commune idea, the comment section started to become a recruitment board, where people were apparently forming joint operations together right in there. [Communes Are Hot Again 🔥]
old: It was chaotic, but sincere, and it revealed to me how people are so ready for this that they’ll literally jump into it from one video.

quote: And what rights does a full member have to the land, the shared resources and a voice in the group, and what do they owe over the long term?
heading: From Visitor to Member—Slowly
said_already: Then you’ll need to decide who has what voting rights, who has what access and use rights to common resources, how you will account for people’s contributions (if at all), how inheritance works, outside debts… oh my! [Money, Land, and Shared Resources]

quote: If it gets to the point of being impossible to live with, they will be kicked out.
heading: From Visitor to Member—Slowly
said_already: If someone is a serious or generalized danger to others, or keeps violating essential boundaries, or for whatever reason just makes everyday life together impossible for everyone else, it can be the right call to eject them. [When Somebody Has to Go]

quote: On top of that they’ve worked out ways of teaching outsiders, all while coordinating beyond a single village.
heading: Democratic anarcho-communalism actualized
said_already: Outsiders came from all over the world, lived with host families there and learned autonomy by taking part in day to day life. [Exporting Zapatismo via the Escuelita]
old: The Zapatistas are also the closest thing to a whole political-economic example that I found, because their autonomy goes beyond how they vote. They’ve set up their own education and health care, and their own justice, and they run their own collective production. On top of that they’ve worked out ways of teaching outsiders, all while coordinating beyond a single village.
new: The Zapatistas are also the closest thing to a whole political-economic example that I found, because their autonomy goes beyond how they vote. They’ve set up their own education and health care, and their own justice, and they run their own collective production.

quote: (little school)
heading: Exporting Zapatismo via the Escuelita
said_already: Escuelita means “little school.” [The New Age May Dawn Suddenly]
old: For the 10th anniversary of their autonomous governments, the Zapatistas opened up the Escuelita (little school). The goal of the escuelita was to expand their anarcho-communal, spiritual-humanist revolution worldwide. Outsiders came from all over the world, lived with host families there and learned autonomy by taking part in day to day life. Around 1,500 students came to the first sessions, and thousands more came to later ones.

quote: It’s for teaching enough of the social and material system that some people can build somewhere else.
heading: Money is still a problem
said_already: In the same way, people would live in the healing communities I’m proposing, to heal and to learn the relational and practical methods, so that some of them could eventually leave and set up another one somewhere else. [The New Age May Dawn Suddenly]
old: One way an escuelita could fail is if it becomes a business, where residents spend their lives performing community for paying outsiders, and success gets measured by how many people come instead of how many daughter communities there are. A week of feeling transformed isn’t what it’s for. It’s for teaching enough of the social and material system that some people can build somewhere else.

quote: So yes, it’s possible for a society to be spiritually alive, generous, funny and super communal, while still becoming cruel to those who break its social categories.
heading: All is not well in paradise
said_already: Does this mean I think Sénégal is some magical place that’s kept its communal paradise? No, not quite. The warmth has hard limits here. [All is not well in paradise]
old: So yes, it’s possible for a society to be spiritually alive, generous, funny and super communal, while still becoming cruel to those who break its social categories. Being in community isn’t automatically liberating. It all depends on who is allowed to belong without pretending.
new: Being in community isn’t automatically liberating. It all depends on who is allowed to belong without pretending.

quote: All of the warnings in this article apply to me, too.
heading: A Hope For Humanity
said_already: I’ve seen founderism in many communes that I’ve visited, and I can see it playing out if I were to be a founder as well. I’ve got all these proposals and visions here in my guides, and so it would be very easy for me to become the person who decides whether or not everyone else “understood” them correctly, even while I wish to remain humble and open to the input of all involved. [Founderism: The Four Questions]
old: I am not currently recruiting anyone or founding a community, which makes it easier for me to write an article like this, since I’m not trying to get you onto my land. I do plan to find some land, and people may naturally end up living around me. All of the warnings in this article apply to me, too. Based on the folks who’ve so far expressed interest, I’m planning to call my commune, “Uncle Joe’s Crazy Farm.” 🤪 Hopefully not gonna be another Trungpa Rinpoche cult.

quote: Note, Pl/ork means play + work.
heading: The Four Parts That Have to Pl/ork Together
said_already: The most important pl/ork (play + work) doesn’t need land anyway. [Practicing Community Can Start Now]

quote: The idea is that the capacity to be there for people when they need help isn’t located in one professional or guru, or the founder of the group that everyone emotionally depends on, but in the community as a whole.
heading: 2. Relational pl/ork
said_already: In the model I’m imagining, some of the functions that are outsourced to therapists in modern society are distributed throughout the community. [The Math of Absorption]

quote: Just because it’s optional participating in the ceremonies doesn’t mean they don’t have to work with the other parts.
heading: 3. Medicine pl/ork
said_already: nobody has to take medicine to have equal respect in the community. But medicine is an optional part of the overall therapy process, and if a member is avoiding the therapy process and becoming hard to deal with, they will naturally not belong at a certain point. [From Visitor to Member—Slowly]

quote: These are less exciting topics to discuss spiritually. It’s rare to see someone come back from an ecstatic vision with news of how to revamp the community’s policies on provisional members, or how to divvy up assets with a departing member, or how to prevent one founder from having control over the land, or what to do when a child reports something serious. And if they do, it’s still something that needs a sober thinking-through.
heading: 4. The container
said_already: Communities tend to focus on the aspect of their project that was most interesting to the original founders, for example political types getting super into writing by-laws, or spiritual types just meditating all the time, or therapists processing each other, or people who like psychedelics discovering they’re all God together and never getting to the point of deciding who will put their name on the deed. [The Four Parts That Have to Pl/ork Together]

quote: They do also attract people who are all for revelation and hate the follow-through, people who can collect 12 ceremonies and 6 origin stories and still can’t say sorry to their housemate.
heading: The Case Against Psychedelics
said_already: This prerequisite also takes care of another issue in one shot: it weeds out the experience collectors. If someone is unwilling to put in 6 months learning to listen without imposing their solution, it is unlikely they will come out of a ceremony more relationally mature [Integration Starts Well Before Ceremony]

quote: Any community based mainly around the peak experience is going to find out sooner or later that the insight doesn’t do the practical work for it.
heading: The Case Against Psychedelics
said_already: It’s rare to see someone come back from an ecstatic vision with news of how to revamp the community’s policies on provisional members, or how to divvy up assets with a departing member, or how to prevent one founder from having control over the land, or what to do when a child reports something serious. [4. The container]

quote: And the more deeply someone is opening up, the more it costs not to personally know who’s running their ceremony.
heading: No Special Shamans
said_already: Support from people you trust is different from paid support, which is often paying people you don’t know to look after you for a night. [Community Is What Makes Psychedelics Pl/ork Best!]

quote: In fact, if people are training there so they can help others build communities of their own, they’d be working towards forming a real alternative.
heading: After the Psychedelic Calling
said_already: A community can be a place for people to train up in the practices, and sometimes go off and start another experiment. [After the Psychedelic Calling]
old: Once the euphoria wears off and people have a more sober view of the call they feel, it can become useful. A community can be a place for people to train up in the practices, and sometimes go off and start another experiment. In fact, if people are training there so they can help others build communities of their own, they’d be working towards forming a real alternative. That answers the reasonable objection that communes are just privileged escape pods, which gets double dipped with the objection that psychedelics are also privileged escape pods (or, alternatively, as some say, “a vacation for the poor”).

quote: There are some ways the group can help, and basic boundaries the group can enforce, without deciding what type of relationships people have.
heading: Jealousy Can Capture Monogamy or Free Love
said_already: I don’t think it should be up to the community to decide for everyone what form relationships will take. People can make different agreements with each other, in pairs, threes, fours, whatever. They can change those agreements as they wish. And they can ask for support when those agreements bring up old material. [Jealousy Can Capture Monogamy or Free Love]
old: There are some ways the group can help, and basic boundaries the group can enforce, without deciding what type of relationships people have. Even so, there will still be disagreements about this.
new: Even so, there will still be disagreements about this.

quote: Kids can benefit from high-quality group care and multiple loving adults in their lives, but replacing a secure attachment to their parents is a different matter.
heading: Communal Parenting Adds On
said_already: My own bias is still toward a system where kids are not solely taken care of by their parents, while still honoring the parent-child bond. [Children Need Freedom Inside Real Protection]
old: Experiments where kids sleep and live apart from their parents deserve special caution. Research on Israeli kibbutzim found that the practice of kids sleeping communally eventually ended due to developmental findings, parents’ preferences and social change. Kids can benefit from high-quality group care and multiple loving adults in their lives, but replacing a secure attachment to their parents is a different matter.

quote: Nobody’s status buys silence.
heading: Children Need Freedom Inside Real Protection
said_already: Hear the child even when the accused is someone people love. Communities fail here, because the adult may be charismatic, useful, rich, spiritually important, or everybody’s friend. [Children Need Freedom Inside Real Protection]

quote: What do members owe one another? What happens when someone wants to leave?
heading: Moving Beyond Money
said_already: Then you’ll need to decide who has what voting rights, who has what access and use rights to common resources, how you will account for people’s contributions (if at all), how inheritance works, outside debts… oh my! Read the founderism questions next, and agree on the exit terms in “Leaving, Removal, and Dissolution” before anyone commits. [Money, Land, and Shared Resources]

Even in a moneyless community, someone can control what’s scarce. Who decides how these things are budgeted and distributed? What do members owe one another? What happens when someone wants to leave?

quote: , and also keeps the differences alive, so communities can keep learning from one another
heading: From One Community to a Movement
said_already: Cooperation also shouldn’t slide into assimilation. The FEC has full members and communities working toward full membership, and Friends who may just want to stay friends. Fortunately, the interface between communities can often be thin, saying who’s responsible for what while somebody crosses between them, and communities don’t have to have the same internal systems for it to work. [From One Community to a Movement]

quote: If the legal or economic environment requires money, the federation also needs to have a cash budget for dealing with it.
heading: From One Community to a Movement
old: The Federation of Egalitarian Communities (FEC) says it’s rebuilding, and that’s a good warning. It takes work to run a federation. Delegates. Records. Compliance. Coordinating resources. Holding meetings. Succession. Whatever dispute function it actually takes on. These things all take up labor and material capacity before any local crisis has eaten into both. If the legal or economic environment requires money, the federation also needs to have a cash budget for dealing with it. But the work of federation doesn’t have to be done by a single entity. Two communities might want to be closely linked as friends, and that doesn’t stop both of them from also being part of a general federation. There can also be local clusters, or single-function institutions like the FEC’s PEACH health pool, which isn’t currently governed by the FEC delegates.

quote: Splitting off completely should be just one step along that gradient, and nobody should have to do it just to be allowed to experiment.
heading: Experiment Before You Split Off
said_already: Experimenting with a different rule doesn’t have to mean everybody goes out and buys new land right away. [Experiment Before You Split Off]
old: Experimenting with a different rule doesn’t have to mean everybody goes out and buys new land right away. Try it inside the parent group first, then as a semi-autonomous project, and then, if it needs more independence, as a seed group nearby that still shares some tools, childcare, business or friendships. Splitting off completely should be just one step along that gradient, and nobody should have to do it just to be allowed to experiment.

quote: That’s coercive -- they HAVE to stay if they can’t afford to go, and a community of prisoners isn’t ideal.
heading: Leaving Voluntarily
said_already: Otherwise their “right” to leave is only on paper -- it only works when the community happens to have spare money. [Leaving Voluntarily]
old: Good people leave for good reasons -- dying parent, love, work, health, exhaustion, change of mind, etc. You don’t want them to lose everything they’ve put in. That’s coercive -- they HAVE to stay if they can’t afford to go, and a community of prisoners isn’t ideal. Whether or not you use money, you’ll need to have a way of providing people with resources when they leave (cash, if you use it, but also tools, transportation, temporary housing, stored up goods, the right to keep using something, or whatever). Otherwise their “right” to leave is only on paper -- it only works when the community happens to have spare money. Write up the exit terms while leaving is still only theoretical -- like a pre-nup when you’re planning the wedding. Not romantic, but protective. Much easier than doing it once anybody’s furious.

quote: , its practice-before-theory approach, how it built autonomous institutions, and the original Good Government Boards
heading: For the Zapatistas
said_already: The Fire and the Word describes the movement growing from family to village, village to region, and region to larger structures. It also gives one of the most useful Zapatista principles for community design: build the practice first and develop the theory afterward. The autonomous municipalities came first; an association of them became a rehearsal for the Good Government Juntas (Boards). [Democratic anarcho-communalism actualized]
